> A tree is a hypothesis about history. Software will give you one whether or
> not your data contains any.

## Learning objectives

1. Build a maximum-likelihood tree.
2. Explain what a bootstrap value does and does not measure.
3. Choose and justify a substitution model.
4. Explain why recombination breaks tree-based methods.

## The alignment determines everything

::: {.callout-important}
## Garbage alignment, garbage tree
Tree-building assumes column *i* is homologous across all sequences. If the
alignment is wrong, every downstream inference is wrong — and the tree will
still look perfectly reasonable.

Look at your alignment. Ragged ends and gap-rich columns are where errors live.
:::

## Substitution models

Not all changes are equally likely. Transitions outnumber transversions; base
composition is uneven; sites evolve at different rates.

| Model | Assumes |
|---|---|
| JC69 | All substitutions equal (rarely true) |
| HKY | Transitions ≠ transversions |
| GTR | All six rates differ |
| +G | Rate varies across sites |
| +I | Some sites invariant |

GTR+G is a reasonable default for viral data. Use ModelFinder rather than
guessing — and report what you used.

## What bootstrap values mean

A bootstrap resamples alignment columns, rebuilds the tree, and asks how often
each clade recurs. High values mean **the data support this clade
consistently.**

::: {.callout-warning}
## Bootstrap measures consistency, not truth
A bootstrap of 100 on a systematically wrong alignment means the error is
consistent. Bootstrap cannot detect bias — only noise.

It also says nothing about whether your model was right, your sampling was
representative, or recombination occurred.
:::

Rough reading: >95 strong, 70–95 moderate, <70 do not interpret.

## Recombination breaks trees

A tree assumes one history for the whole sequence. A recombinant has two.
Forcing it into a single tree produces a topology that is wrong everywhere.

::: {.callout-important}
## Test for recombination first
If [Module 3](3-genotyping.qmd) found breakpoints, do not build one tree.
Split at the breakpoints and build a tree per segment. Different segments give
different — and both correct — topologies.
:::

## Trees are not epidemiology

A clade means sequences are similar. It does not mean transmission. Similar
viruses cluster for many reasons: shared source, sampling, convergent
evolution. Transmission inference needs dates, and usually more.

## Exercises

1. Build a tree with IQ-TREE and 1,000 bootstraps. Which nodes are supported?
2. Compare JC69 to GTR+G. Does the topology change? Does support?
3. Take a recombinant, build one tree, then per-segment trees. Compare.
4. *Discussion.* Two sequences sit together with bootstrap 99. A colleague
   concludes direct transmission. What do you say?

## Takeaways

- Inspect the alignment first.
- Bootstrap measures consistency, not correctness.
- Test recombination before building a tree.
- Clustering is not transmission.
